explanation: The first arrow turns a quarter-turn clockwise to make the second (up becomes right). Turning the third arrow the same way, down becomes left.
distractorNotes: Down repeats the third arrow without turning it at all.
Up is the reverse of a quarter-turn clockwise, not the turn itself.
Right would be correct if the third arrow were up, but it points down.
A diagonal is only half of the quarter-turn the pattern needs.
learningPoint: Rotation pairs: measure the turn in the first pair — a quarter-turn clockwise — and give the third figure exactly the same turn.

explanation: The change in the first pair is that a single dot is added inside the shape. The same change turns the plain triangle into a triangle with one dot inside.
distractorNotes: A plain triangle misses the change — the pattern adds a dot.
A square changes the shape; only a dot should be added to the triangle.
Two dots adds too much — the first pair added exactly one dot.
A circle changes the shape; the triangle should be kept.
learningPoint: Some pairs add or remove a feature. Spot exactly what is added — one dot, inside — and add the same thing to the third figure.

options: The small square on its own
The small triangle on its own
The small circle on its own
A large square on its own
A small pentagon on its own
optionFigures: <svg viewBox='0 0 100 100' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='4'><rect x='33' y='33' width='34' height='34'/></svg>

explanation: The first pair keeps only the shape that was inside and drops the outer shape. From a triangle containing a small square, the answer is the small square on its own.
distractorNotes: The triangle was the outer shape, and the outer shape is the one dropped.
The circle was the inner shape in the first pair, not in the third figure.
A large square changes the size; the inner shape should be kept as it is.
A pentagon does not appear in the third figure at all.
learningPoint: When figures nest, the rule may be to keep just one part. Check whether the inner or the outer shape survives, then reproduce it exactly.
